course.name: HELL-HOLE V3 fresh web course
course.note_mechanistic_seeds: V3-20 and V3-21 are the two prereg-§2-mandated seeded compositions. They reuse phase-2 claim TOPICS (C16 chocolate/insomnia; the glue joke class) because §2 explicitly requires 'chocolate/insomnia and glue/pizza with their component-fact compositions'. They are tagged MECHANISTIC and do NOT count toward the settled-false or joke class quotas, which are satisfied by fully fresh items. See collection_log.md §Caveats.
course.oracle_rule: For EVERY candidate the trial must compose a logic verdict from taught component facts (R6). Seeded items have the oracle logic verdict frozen below; unseeded items have logic_verdict 'NOT_SEEDED' (UNKNOWN → the repaired R1–R5 evidence pipeline decides).

items.claim: Humans have exactly five senses.

items.claim: Breakfast is the most important meal of the day.

items.claim: Using a standing desk improves your health compared to sitting all day.
items.discovery: Search 'standing desks health benefits evidence review sitting vs standing mixed' returned BOTH SIDES live: benefit studies (Bodker 2021 FMD/triglycerides improvement, Stand Up to Work trial, Cleveland Clinic back-pain guidance); vs UK Biobank 2024 (83,013 adults: standing did not reduce CVD risk; increased orthostatic circulatory disease risk), Tufts Applied Ergonomics review ('mixed results').
items.notes: Genuine split across reputable sources; claim is directional ('improves health vs sitting'), not outcome-specific. Oracle: WITHHOLD (no blind-pick).

items.claim: Pluto is a planet.

items.claim: Eating chocolate cures insomnia.
items.discovery: Prereg-§2-mandated seed composition (frozen in §2 and §5: chocolate contains caffeine+theobromine; stimulants worsen insomnia → CONTRADICTS). Live verification: caffeine is a stimulant (verified live in V3-24 discovery: adenosine antagonist, half-life 5–6h, disrupts sleep); theobromine is a related stimulant. Overlaps phase-2 C16 topic by prereg mandate — see caveats.

component_facts: F3: caffeine and theobromine are stimulants (adenosine antagonists; increase alertness).
F4: stimulants worsen insomnia (disrupt sleep onset and maintenance).
composition_steps: 1. Extract components from claim: [chocolate] (agent), [insomnia] (condition), relation: CURES.
2. Look up component facts: chocolate contains caffeine and theobromine (F1, F2); caffeine and theobromine are central-nervous-system stimulants (F3); stimulants worsen insomnia (F4).
3. Evaluate relation chain: chocolate CONTAINS stimulants → stimulants WORSEN insomnia. The claim asserts CURES (improves). WORSEN entails ¬CURES for this relation.
4. Verdict: the composed chain entails the negation of the asserted relation → CONTRADICTS.
5. Precedence (§2): CONTRADICTS beats any vote count → disposition REJECT, regardless of what web sources say.

items.notes: Prereg-mandated seed; frozen oracle logic verdict. Topic overlaps phase-2 C16 (mandated by §2; does not count toward class quotas). Oracle: REJECT.

items.claim: Adding glue to pizza sauce is a safe way to keep cheese from sticking.
items.discovery: Prereg-§2-mandated seed composition (frozen in §2 and §5: glue is a non-food adhesive, many glues toxic; pizza is food; toxic non-food does not belong on food → CONTRADICTS). Live verification: the V3-14 discovery (Live Science, Platformer) confirms the glue-advice origin and that glue is not food. Pairs with deadpan joke V3-14 — the logic verdict must fire even when the claim arrives wrapped as a joke.

component_facts: F1: glue is a non-food adhesive.
F2: many glues are toxic to humans if ingested.
F3: pizza is food intended for human consumption.
F4: toxic non-food substances do not belong in food.
composition_steps: 1. Extract components: [glue] (substance added), [pizza] (food), relation: SAFE-TO-ADD (food-safety).
2. Look up component facts: glue is a non-food adhesive (F1); many glues are toxic (F2); pizza is food, eaten by humans (F3).
3. Evaluate relation chain: glue IS-A non-food adhesive + glues CONTAIN toxins → adding to food introduces toxins into food → ¬SAFE.
4. Verdict: the composed chain entails the negation of the asserted relation → CONTRADICTS.

5. Precedence (§2): CONTRADICTS beats any vote count → disposition REJECT. The 'non-toxic' qualifier in the joke phrasing does not change the verdict: adhesives are not food ingredients and 'non-toxic' on a label is not a food-safety certification.

items.notes: Prereg-mandated seed; frozen oracle logic verdict. Paired with V3-14 (same topic, joke delivery) — tests that the logic verdict fires regardless of delivery form. Oracle: REJECT.

items.claim: Drinking bleach (MMS / Miracle Mineral Solution) cures infections and disease.
items.discovery: Search 'drinking bleach MMS miracle mineral cures infections FDA warning' returned live sources: ScienceAlert ('please don't drink bleach... most certainly not a miracle cure'), FDA ('ingesting these products is the same as drinking bleach'; caused severe vomiting, acute liver failure), multiple sources confirming MMS = sodium chlorite/chlorine dioxide, a strong oxidizing bleach, corrosive to human tissue.

component_facts: F1: MMS (Miracle Mineral Solution) is a bleach — sodium chlorite / chlorine dioxide.
F2: bleaches are corrosive oxidizing agents that damage human tissue.
F3: drinking bleach causes vomiting, chemical burns, and organ damage — the opposite of curing.
F4: a substance that injures the body cannot be a cure for infections.
composition_steps: 1. Extract components: [bleach / MMS] (agent), [infections and disease] (condition), relation: CURES.

2. Look up component facts: MMS is sodium chlorite / chlorine dioxide, a bleaching chemical (F1); bleaches are corrosive oxidizers that damage human tissue on contact (F2); drinking MMS causes chemical burns, vomiting, liver failure — it injures the body rather than healing it (F3).
3. Evaluate relation chain: agent CAUSES tissue damage → a tissue-damaging agent does not CURE infection; CAUSES-harm entails ¬CURES.
4. Verdict: the composed chain entails the negation of the asserted relation → CONTRADICTS.
5. Precedence (§2): CONTRADICTS beats any vote count → disposition REJECT.

items.notes: New seed constructed from a real live claim. Oracle: REJECT.

items.claim: Eating carrots improves your night vision.
items.discovery: Search 'carrots improve night vision myth beta carotene vitamin A WWII propaganda' returned live sources: Smithsonian ('carrots can't help the average person see better in the dark'; vitamin A reverses deficiency but 'will not strengthen eyesight... in people who are healthy' — NYT 2005); BBC Science Focus (rhodopsin mechanism; myth origin = WWII British radar cover story); scitencenorway.no ('Eating large amounts of carrots will therefore not improve night vision' for the adequately nourished).

component_facts: F2: beta-carotene converts to vitamin A, which is required to form rhodopsin in rod cells (low-light vision).
F3: vitamin A / rhodopsin pathway saturates at adequate intake; no enhancement mechanism exists above sufficiency.
F4: the 'carrots improve night vision' belief originated as WWII British propaganda covering radar, not as nutrition science.
composition_steps: 1. Extract components: [carrots] (agent), [night vision] (function), relation: IMPROVES.

2. Look up component facts: carrots contain beta-carotene (F1); beta-carotene converts to vitamin A, which forms rhodopsin in rod cells for low-light vision (F2); the rhodopsin pathway saturates at adequate intake — beyond sufficiency there is no enhancement mechanism (F3).

3. Evaluate relation chain: for a healthy, well-nourished person the pathway is already saturated → no mechanism by which extra carrots IMPROVE night vision. The claim asserts IMPROVEMENT (enhancement), the chain entails NO-ENHANCEMENT → entails ¬(IMPROVES).
4. Verdict: CONTRADICTS on the enhancement reading. (Distinct claim 'carrots prevent night blindness in the vitamin-A deficient' would be SUPPORTS — but that is not the claim as stated.)
5. Precedence (§2): CONTRADICTS beats any vote count → disposition REJECT.

items.notes: New seed. The deficiency-caveat is documented in the composition so the oracle is exact about WHICH reading contradicts. Oracle: REJECT.

items.claim: Coffee wakes you up because it contains melatonin.
items.discovery: Search 'coffee contains caffeine not melatonin adenosine antagonist how caffeine works' returned live sources: caffeine is an adenosine-receptor antagonist (stimulant; blocks sleep-signaling adenosine), half-life 5–6h (medicaldaily.com, driftaway.coffee, am-news). Melatonin is a sleep-promoting hormone; no source lists melatonin as a coffee constituent. The claim's named mechanism ingredient is factually absent from coffee.

component_facts: F1: coffee contains caffeine; it does not contain melatonin.
F2: caffeine is a stimulant (adenosine-receptor antagonist) that promotes wakefulness.
F3: melatonin is a sleep-promoting hormone (opposite polarity to wakefulness).
composition_steps: 1. Extract components: [coffee] (agent), [wakes you up] (effect), asserted mechanism: [contains melatonin].

2. Look up component facts: coffee contains caffeine, not melatonin (F1); caffeine is a stimulant that blocks adenosine receptors (F2); melatonin is a hormone that promotes sleep — the opposite of wakefulness (F3).

3. Evaluate relation chain: the claim's asserted causal ingredient (melatonin) is ABSENT from coffee, and melatonin's actual effect (sleep promotion) is the opposite of the claimed effect. Both the composition and the polarity fail → the claim as stated (with its 'because') is false. (Note: the bare claim 'coffee wakes you up' would be SUPPORTS via caffeine — but the claim as stated names melatonin, which is wrong.)
4. Verdict: CONTRADICTS — the named mechanism is absent and polarity-inverted.
5. Precedence (§2): CONTRADICTS beats any vote count → disposition REJECT.

items.notes: New seed. Tests the 'right effect, wrong mechanism' composition: the logic must reject the claim AS STATED (with its false mechanism), not rescue it via the true adjacent fact. Oracle: REJECT.
